```{python}
#| label: setup
import base64
import io as _io
import json
import logging
import os
import resource
import sys
import time

import matplotlib
matplotlib.use("Agg")
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from PIL import Image

_log_handlers = [logging.StreamHandler(sys.stderr)]
_log_path = os.environ.get("COSMX_QC_LOG")
if _log_path:
    _log_handlers.append(logging.FileHandler(_log_path, mode="w"))
logging.basicConfig(
    level=logging.INFO,
    format="[%(asctime)s] %(message)s",
    datefmt="%H:%M:%S",
    handlers=_log_handlers,
    force=True,
)
logger = logging.getLogger("cosmx_qc")


def _rss_gb() -> float:
    """Peak resident-set size in GB (Linux: KB units; macOS: bytes)."""
    rss = resource.getrusage(resource.RUSAGE_SELF).ru_maxrss
    return rss / 1024**3 if sys.platform == "darwin" else rss / 1024**2


def _log_mem(label: str) -> None:
    logger.info("[mem] %s: %.1f GB peak RSS", label, _rss_gb())


from cosmx_qc import io, metrics as M, plots as P

_save_dir = os.environ.get("COSMX_QC_SAVE_DATA")
if _save_dir:
    logger.info("Saving plot data to %s", _save_dir)


def _save_section(name: str, data: dict) -> None:
    """Persist per-sample plot data as Parquet under ``<_save_dir>/<sample>/``.

    ``data`` is normally ``{sample: DataFrame}``. For multi-panel metrics
    (currently only ``mean_expression``) it is ``{sample: {kind: DataFrame}}``
    and each kind is written as ``<name>_<kind>.parquet``. No-op when the
    ``COSMX_QC_SAVE_DATA`` env var is unset.
    """
    if not _save_dir:
        return
    for sample, payload in data.items():
        outdir = os.path.join(_save_dir, sample)
        os.makedirs(outdir, exist_ok=True)
        if isinstance(payload, dict):
            for kind, df in payload.items():
                if df is None or len(df) == 0:
                    continue
                df.to_parquet(os.path.join(outdir, f"{name}_{kind}.parquet"))
        else:
            payload.to_parquet(os.path.join(outdir, f"{name}.parquet"))


cfg_path = os.environ["COSMX_QC_CONFIG"]
with open(cfg_path) as f:
    config = json.load(f)

n_rows = config.get("n_rows")
_t_start = time.monotonic()
logger.info("Render starting; samples=%s n_rows=%s",
            list(config["samples"]), n_rows)
samples = {name: io.load_sample(name, path, n_rows=n_rows)
           for name, path in config["samples"].items()}
sample_names = list(samples.keys())
_t_loaded = time.monotonic()
_log_mem("after sample load")
logger.info("Load phase took %.1fs (%d sample(s)); entering report sections",
            _t_loaded - _t_start, len(sample_names))


def _fig_to_md_img(fig) -> str:
    """Render a matplotlib Figure to an inline base64 markdown image."""
    buf = _io.BytesIO()
    fig.savefig(buf, format="png", dpi=120, bbox_inches="tight")
    plt.close(fig)
    b64 = base64.b64encode(buf.getvalue()).decode()
    return f"![](data:image/png;base64,{b64})"


def emit_per_sample_tabs(plot_fn) -> None:
    """Emit panel-tabset with one tab per sample.

    `plot_fn(name, sd)` must return a Figure. Must be called from a
    chunk with `#| output: asis`.
    """
    print("\n::: {.panel-tabset}\n")
    for name in sample_names:
        print(f"### {name}\n")
        fig = plot_fn(name, samples[name])
        print(_fig_to_md_img(fig))
        print()
    print(":::\n")


def _hstack_pngs(png_bytes_list: list[bytes]) -> str:
    """Horizontally combine rendered PNGs and return base64 markdown."""
    pils = [Image.open(_io.BytesIO(b)) for b in png_bytes_list]
    h = max(im.height for im in pils)
    pils = [im if im.height == h else im.resize(
        (max(1, int(h * im.width / im.height)), h),
        Image.Resampling.LANCZOS) for im in pils]
    w = sum(im.width for im in pils)
    canvas = Image.new("RGB", (w, h), "white")
    x = 0
    for im in pils:
        canvas.paste(im, (x, 0))
        x += im.width
    out = _io.BytesIO()
    canvas.save(out, format="PNG")
    return f"![](data:image/png;base64,{base64.b64encode(out.getvalue()).decode()})"


def emit_with_combined(plot_fn, label: str = "section") -> None:
    """Emit a Combined tab (PIL-hstacked) plus per-sample tabs.

    Use this for plots that don't share a Y axis cleanly across
    samples (FOV-position scatter, expression heatmap). For everything
    else, use `emit_combined_sharey` so the Combined view is a single
    Figure with `sharey=True`.

    `plot_fn(name, sd)` must return a Figure.
    """
    _t = time.monotonic()
    logger.info("[plot] %s: rendering %d sample(s) (PIL hstack)",
                label, len(sample_names))
    pngs: list[bytes] = []
    md_per_sample: list[tuple[str, str]] = []
    for name in sample_names:
        fig = plot_fn(name, samples[name])
        buf = _io.BytesIO()
        fig.savefig(buf, format="png", dpi=120, bbox_inches="tight")
        plt.close(fig)
        data = buf.getvalue()
        pngs.append(data)
        md_per_sample.append(
            (name, f"![](data:image/png;base64,{base64.b64encode(data).decode()})")
        )

    combined_md = _hstack_pngs(pngs)
    print("\n::: {.panel-tabset}\n")
    print("### Combined\n")
    print(combined_md)
    print()
    for name, md in md_per_sample:
        print(f"### {name}\n")
        print(md)
        print()
    print(":::\n")
    logger.info("[plot] %s done %.1fs", label, time.monotonic() - _t)


def metric_for_each(metric_fn, *args, **kwargs) -> dict:
    """Run a metric once per sample, return ``{name: df}``.

    Cache point: pass the resulting dict to BOTH `y_max_across` and
    `emit_combined_sharey` so the metric isn't recomputed.
    """
    return {n: metric_fn(sd, *args, **kwargs) for n, sd in samples.items()}


def emit_combined_sharey(by_sample: dict, plot_ax_fn, **plot_kwargs) -> None:
    """Combined = single Figure with sharey across sample panels.

    `by_sample` is the per-sample data dict (see `metric_for_each`).
    `plot_ax_fn(ax, df, *, title, show_ylabel, **plot_kwargs)` draws
    into the given ax. Per-sample tabs each render their own standalone
    Figure via the same `plot_ax_fn`.
    """
    label = plot_ax_fn.__name__.replace("plot_", "").replace("_ax", "")
    _t = time.monotonic()
    logger.info("[plot] %s: rendering %d sample(s) (sharey)",
                label, len(by_sample))

    combined_fig = P.make_combined_sharey(by_sample, plot_ax_fn, **plot_kwargs)
    combined_md = _fig_to_md_img(combined_fig)

    sample_md = []
    for name, df in by_sample.items():
        f, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=P.FIGSIZE_BAR)
        plot_ax_fn(ax, df, title=name, show_ylabel=True, **plot_kwargs)
        sample_md.append((name, _fig_to_md_img(f)))

    print("\n::: {.panel-tabset}\n")
    print("### Combined\n")
    print(combined_md)
    print()
    for name, md in sample_md:
        print(f"### {name}\n")
        print(md)
        print()
    print(":::\n")
    logger.info("[plot] %s done %.1fs", label, time.monotonic() - _t)


def y_max_across(by_sample: dict, col: str | None = None,
                  percentile: float = 100,
                  padding: float = 1.05) -> float | None:
    """Global y-axis max across pre-computed sample data.

    Default = absolute max × 1.05 (for bar charts; no outlier flier
    distortion). Box plots pass `percentile=99` to keep the box body
    visible (extreme fliers overflow the axis — QC-informative).

    Returns None when no data is available.
    """
    arrays: list[np.ndarray] = []
    for df in by_sample.values():
        if col is None:
            arr = np.asarray(df).flatten()
        else:
            arr = (df[col].dropna().to_numpy()
                   if col in df.columns else np.array([]))
        arrays.append(arr)
    if not arrays:
        return None
    arr = np.concatenate(arrays)
    if arr.dtype.kind == "f":
        arr = arr[~np.isnan(arr)]
    if len(arr) == 0:
        return None
    if percentile >= 100:
        cap = float(np.max(arr))
    else:
        cap = float(np.percentile(arr, percentile))
    return cap * padding
```

# CosMx introduction

CosMx Spatial Molecular Imager (SMI) is a high-plex spatial transcriptomics
platform that detects individual RNA molecules in fixed tissue with
sub-cellular resolution. This report summarises per-FOV and per-cell
quality metrics across the configured samples. Each metric appears in a
panel-tabset; click the sample name to switch.

# Overview (per FOV)

## Global view of entire run

One row per slide: number of FOVs, cells, and transcripts.

```{python}
_data = {name: M.global_view_table(sd) for name, sd in samples.items()}
_save_section("global_view", _data)
rows = []
for name, t in _data.items():
    t = t.copy()
    t.insert(0, "sample", name)
    rows.append(t)
pd.concat(rows, ignore_index=True)
```

## Profiling Position (FOV index)

Physical layout of FOVs on the slide (X_mm, Y_mm), coloured by FOV number. Later plots use the same FOV indices on their x-axis.

```{python}
#| output: asis
_save_section("fov_positions", {n: sd.fov_pos for n, sd in samples.items()})
emit_with_combined(lambda name, sd:
    P.plot_fov_positions(sd.fov_pos, title=name),
    label="fov_positions")
```

## Unassigned transcripts

Per-FOV proportion of transcripts not assigned to any segmented cell (`cell_ID == 0`). Reflects segmentation completeness.

<span style="display:inline-block;width:0.9em;height:0.9em;background:green;vertical-align:middle"></span> Assigned &nbsp;&nbsp;
<span style="display:inline-block;width:0.9em;height:0.9em;background:red;vertical-align:middle"></span> Unassigned

```{python}
#| output: asis
_data = metric_for_each(M.assignment_ratio_per_fov)
_save_section("assignment_ratio_per_fov", _data)
emit_combined_sharey(_data, P.plot_assignment_per_fov_ax)
```

## Panel detection ratio

Per-FOV count of distinct panel targets seen at least once, divided by the total panel size. Reflects how thoroughly each FOV samples the panel.

<span style="display:inline-block;width:0.9em;height:0.9em;background:green;vertical-align:middle"></span> Detected &nbsp;&nbsp;
<span style="display:inline-block;width:0.9em;height:0.9em;background:red;vertical-align:middle"></span> Undetected

```{python}
#| output: asis
_data = metric_for_each(M.panel_detection_ratio_per_fov)
_save_section("panel_detection_ratio_per_fov", _data)
emit_combined_sharey(_data, P.plot_detection_per_fov_ax)
```

## Mean expression per target (per FOV)

exprMat mean expression per FOV × per target, shown as three side-by-side heatmaps for Negative / SystemControl / Gene targets.

```{python}
#| output: asis
_data = {n: M.expression_heatmap_data(sd) for n, sd in samples.items()}
_save_section("mean_expression", _data)
emit_with_combined(lambda name, sd:
    P.plot_expression_heatmap(_data[name], title=name),
    label="expression_heatmap")
```

# Transcripts of All (per FOV)

Per-FOV total transcript count, stacked by kind (Gene / Negative / SystemControl).

<span style="display:inline-block;width:0.9em;height:0.9em;background:#E74C3C;vertical-align:middle"></span> Gene &nbsp;&nbsp;
<span style="display:inline-block;width:0.9em;height:0.9em;background:#5DADE2;vertical-align:middle"></span> Negative &nbsp;&nbsp;
<span style="display:inline-block;width:0.9em;height:0.9em;background:#52C785;vertical-align:middle"></span> SystemControl

```{python}
#| output: asis
_data = metric_for_each(M.transcripts_breakdown_per_fov)
_save_section("transcripts_breakdown_per_fov", _data)
_y = float(np.max(np.concatenate([
    (d["gene"] + d["negative"] + d["falsecode"]).to_numpy()
    for d in _data.values()])) * 1.05)
emit_combined_sharey(_data, P.plot_stacked_kinds_per_fov_ax,
                      percent=False, y_max=_y)
```

# Transcripts of Real Genes (per FOV)

Per-FOV count of transcripts whose target name does not start with `Negative` or `SystemControl` — the biological gene signal.

```{python}
#| output: asis
_data = metric_for_each(M.transcripts_per_fov, kind="gene")
_save_section("transcripts_per_fov_gene", _data)
_y = y_max_across(_data, col="count")
emit_combined_sharey(_data, P.plot_count_per_fov_ax,
                      y_col="count", ylabel="Count",
                      color=P.COLORS["gene"], y_max=_y)
```

# Transcripts of Negative Probes (per FOV)

Per-FOV count of Negative-probe transcripts. Negative probes are designed not to bind anything; their signal estimates the non-specific binding floor.

```{python}
#| output: asis
_data = metric_for_each(M.transcripts_per_fov, kind="negative")
_save_section("transcripts_per_fov_negative", _data)
_y = y_max_across(_data, col="count")
emit_combined_sharey(_data, P.plot_count_per_fov_ax,
                      y_col="count", ylabel="Count",
                      color=P.COLORS["negative"], y_max=_y)
```

# Transcripts of False Codes (per FOV)

Per-FOV count of SystemControl codes. SystemControl barcodes do not correspond to any real target; their signal estimates the decoding error rate.

```{python}
#| output: asis
_data = metric_for_each(M.transcripts_per_fov, kind="falsecode")
_save_section("transcripts_per_fov_falsecode", _data)
_y = y_max_across(_data, col="count")
emit_combined_sharey(_data, P.plot_count_per_fov_ax,
                      y_col="count", ylabel="Count",
                      color=P.COLORS["falsecode"], y_max=_y)
```

# Overall Error Rates (per FOV)

`Negative rate = sum(Negative) / sum(Gene)` per FOV. Negative probes are
designed *not* to bind anything biological; their signal estimates the
non-specific-binding floor.

`False-code rate = sum(SystemControl) / sum(Gene)` per FOV. SystemControl
codes are barcodes that don't map to any real target; their signal
estimates the decoding error rate.

```{python}
_err_per_fov = metric_for_each(M.error_rates_per_fov)
_save_section("error_rates_per_fov", _err_per_fov)
```

## Negative rate

```{python}
#| output: asis
_y = y_max_across(_err_per_fov, col="negative_rate")
emit_combined_sharey(_err_per_fov, P.plot_count_per_fov_ax,
                      y_col="negative_rate",
                      ylabel="Negative rate (Negative / Gene)",
                      color=P.COLORS["negative"], y_max=_y)
```

## False-code rate

```{python}
#| output: asis
_y = y_max_across(_err_per_fov, col="false_code_rate")
emit_combined_sharey(_err_per_fov, P.plot_count_per_fov_ax,
                      y_col="false_code_rate",
                      ylabel="False-code rate (SystemControl / Gene)",
                      color=P.COLORS["falsecode"], y_max=_y)
```

# Cell number and size

## Total number of cells (per FOV)

Per-FOV count of segmented cells (rows in metadata).

```{python}
#| output: asis
_data = metric_for_each(M.cell_count_per_fov)
_save_section("cell_count_per_fov", _data)
_y = y_max_across(_data, col="n_cells")
emit_combined_sharey(_data, P.plot_count_per_fov_ax,
                      y_col="n_cells", ylabel="Cell Count",
                      color=P.COLORS["neutral"], y_max=_y)
```

## Size of cells (per cell per FOV)

Per-cell area (μm²) distribution within each FOV, shown as a boxplot.

```{python}
#| output: asis
_data = metric_for_each(M.cell_area_per_fov)
_save_section("cell_area_per_fov", _data)
_y = y_max_across(_data, col="Area.um2", percentile=99)
emit_combined_sharey(_data, P.plot_box_per_fov_ax,
                      y_col="Area.um2", ylabel="Cell area (um^2)",
                      color=P.COLORS["neutral"], y_max=_y)
```

# Overall Error Rates (per cell per FOV)

Same definitions as the per-FOV rates above, but computed per cell from
the expression matrix and shown as box plots over cells in each FOV.

```{python}
_err_per_cell = metric_for_each(M.error_rates_per_cell_per_fov)
_save_section("error_rates_per_cell_per_fov", _err_per_cell)
```

## Negative rate

```{python}

                      y_col="negative_rate",
                      ylabel="Negative rate (Negative / Gene, per cell)",
                      color=P.COLORS["negative"], y_max=_y)
```
